items.title: Parole Board Upgrades Mississauga Man Zakaria Amara to Full Release Two Decades After Toronto Terror Plot
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Zakaria Amara, a Mississauga man who helped recruit members for a group that plotted to storm Parliament Hill and bomb several Toronto-area locations, has been granted full parole. According to the outlet, Amara had already spent four years on day parole under multiple conditions before the board upgraded his release after reviewing his case last week. The outlet says he was closely supervised during that period, with his internet use, friendships and relationships monitored, and no reported safety concerns or breaches. Insauga.com reports Amara remains barred from contacting anyone involved in criminal activity, including others arrested in the June 2006 anti-terrorist raids, or anyone holding extremist ideologies, except through his work as a consultant with a specialized program. The outlet says he must also keep participating in counselling and remain subject to financial monitoring and restrictions on his phone and internet use. Insauga.com notes the board's decision comes two decades after the dismantling of a homegrown plot that shocked the country and shifted public discourse around terrorism.

items.title: Peel Municipalities Fall Behind Ford Government's Housing Targets as Affordability Gap Widens
items.summary: The Pointer reports Mississauga and Brampton now rank among the world's 15 least affordable places to buy a home, even as the province pushes municipalities to build more housing. According to the outlet, Ontario Premier Doug Ford assigned ambitious housing targets to 29 municipalities four years after his election, tasking Mississauga with 120,000 new homes by 2031 and Brampton with 113,000. The Pointer says that mandate was followed by sweeping legislative changes meant to accelerate development, many of which weakened environmental protections and eased restrictions on developers in the name of affordability. The outlet reports all three Peel municipalities are not on track to meet the housing goals the province set for them. The Pointer cites regional data showing 80 per cent of Peel residents cannot afford to buy a home.

items.title: Mississauga Man Identified as Suspect in Yonge Street Attack on Pro-Palestinian Demonstrator
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a 20-year-old Mississauga man, Martin Salgatar, has been charged with aggravated assault after an alleged attack on a demonstrator during a pro-Palestinian rally in downtown Toronto. According to Toronto police, Salgatar surrendered to officers on Oct. 12, two days after the alleged assault near Yonge and Grosvenor streets on Saturday, Oct. 10. Investigators allege the victim was walking northbound on Yonge Street and talking with another demonstrator when the suspect approached from behind and punched the victim several times in the head without provocation. Police say the victim fell to the ground and sustained injuries to the face and leg. The outlet reports the Toronto Police Service's Hate Crime Unit is handling the investigation, which began with a public appeal for help identifying the suspect. Insauga.com says Salgatar was scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Oct. 13.

items.title: Frost Advisory Issued for Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton as Temperatures Dip Toward Freezing Overnight
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Environment Canada has placed Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton under a yellow frost advisory as temperatures are expected to dip toward freezing overnight into Saturday morning. According to the forecaster, areas north of Highway 401 are expected to see temperatures fall to near or slightly below the freezing mark, while neighbourhoods closer to Lake Ontario will stay a few degrees warmer. Environment Canada says the frost could cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The outlet reports Toronto's overnight low is forecast at 0 C, or 3 C near the lake, with a 40 per cent chance of showers Friday evening. Insauga.com says northwest winds are expected to reach 40 km/h and gust to 60 km/h before easing to 20 km/h, gusting to 40 km/h, by morning.

items.title: Four Homes Razed as Edenshaw Breaks Ground on 30-Storey Port Credit Rental Tower
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Edenshaw Developments has broken ground on a 30-storey rental apartment building near the Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga, after demolishing four homes and a shed that previously occupied the site. According to the outlet, the project sits at 23 Elizabeth St. N. and 42-46 Park St., and a spokesperson for Edenshaw said demolition of the existing structures is nearly complete. The outlet reports the development has faced criticism before: a previous application for a 22-storey building on the same property was rejected by the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2023. Insauga.com says the height of the new 30-storey proposal remains a concern for some area residents. The outlet quotes a Facebook post from September in which a resident said surrounding buildings could be affected by privacy and overlook issues, shadow, wind, traffic, and construction dust and noise.

items.title: INSAUGA Poll Finds Mississauga Readers Skeptical a Subway Will Ever Reach the City
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a majority of respondents to its reader poll do not believe Mississauga will ever get a subway, despite billions of dollars being invested in rapid transit in the city. According to the outlet, the poll asked readers whether Mississauga will ever get a subway, and skeptics edged out those who think it will happen by a margin of 441 votes. The outlet notes Mississauga currently has no subway line and there are no announced plans to extend Toronto's subway system into the city. Insauga.com reports the city is nonetheless in the middle of one of the biggest transit transformations in its history. The outlet says the Hazel McCallion Line, formerly known as the Hurontario LRT, is under construction and will run about 18 kilometres between Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga and the Brampton Gateway Terminal at Steeles Avenue.

items.title: Advance Voting Turnout in Mississauga Jumps 57 Percent Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports a record surge in advance voting ahead of the city's Oct. 26 municipal election. According to data the city released Oct. 13, 44,049 residents cast ballots during advance polls held between Oct. 6 and 11, a 57 per cent increase from the 28,052 early voters recorded during the 2022 municipal election's advance polling window. The outlet reports the single busiest day was Oct. 11, when 12,335 ballots were cast. Mississauga.com says advance voting turnout has climbed steadily since 2018, when 19,188 residents voted early, rising to 24,731 during the June 2024 mayoral byelection. The outlet notes residents who missed the advance voting window can still cast a ballot on municipal election day, Oct. 26.
